questions.stem: Which wireless protocol is cryptographically broken and must not be used?
questions.explanation: WEP uses RC4 with a critically short IV, crackable in minutes with freely available tools. Deprecated in 2004.

choices.C: Offline dictionary attacks against captured WPA2 handshakes

questions.explanation: SAE replaces WPA2's PSK with a protocol providing forward secrecy and preventing offline dictionary attacks on captured handshakes.

questions.stem: An evil twin attack works by:

choices.A: Flooding a legitimate AP with deauth frames
choices.B: Cracking the WPA2 passphrase from captured packets
choices.C: Injecting malicious frames into existing associations
choices.D: Broadcasting the same SSID as a legitimate network to intercept connecting clients

questions.explanation: An evil twin AP mimics a legitimate network's SSID. Clients that connect have all traffic routed through the attacker.

questions.stem: WPA2-Enterprise is preferred over WPA2-PSK for enterprise because:

choices.B: Each user authenticates with unique credentials enabling individual accountability and revocation
choices.C: It requires less AP processing power
choices.D: It is immune to deauthentication attacks

questions.explanation: WPA2-Enterprise provides per-user credentials. A terminated employee's account is revoked without changing the password for everyone.

questions.stem: WPS PIN mode is vulnerable to:

choices.D: Brute-force attacks exploiting a design flaw that reduces the keyspace to ~11,000 combinations

questions.explanation: WPS PIN has a design flaw making brute-force feasible in hours, recovering the WPS PIN and then the network passphrase.

questions.stem: Isolating guest wireless on a dedicated VLAN with internet-only access applies:

choices.C: Network segmentation limiting untrusted clients' access to internal resources
choices.D: Defence in depth at the application layer

questions.explanation: VLAN segmentation confines guest devices, even if compromised, they cannot reach internal servers or corporate resources.

choices.B: Forged deauthentication and disassociation frames used in deauth flood attacks

questions.explanation: 802.11w authenticates management frames including deauthentication, preventing attackers from sending forged frames to force disconnections.

choices.B: Physically breaking into buildings for network access
choices.C: Cracking WPA2 passphrases from captured handshakes
choices.D: Planting rogue APs inside target facilities

questions.explanation: Wardriving maps wireless networks, SSIDs, encryption types, signal strength, GPS coordinates, for network reconnaissance.

choices.A: Negligible security, SSIDs still appear in probe requests and are discovered by passive scanners
choices.C: Complete protection against evil twin attacks

questions.explanation: Hidden SSIDs appear in client probe requests and AP management frames. Passive wireless scanners discover them within seconds.

choices.A: Strong authentication because MACs are hardware-bound and unmodifiable
choices.B: Weak security because MAC addresses are transmitted in cleartext and easily spoofed
choices.D: Prevention of all unauthorised device access

questions.explanation: MAC addresses are visible in plaintext in 802.11 frames. An attacker who observes a valid MAC can clone it trivially, defeating MAC filtering.
